cross_module_architecture.issues_preventing_higher_score: App.tsx acts as a hub module containing scene data, presentation logic, and state management in a single file, creating moderate blast radius

cross_module_architecture.dimension_character: The codebase has a clean, unidirectional dependency graph with no cycles or layer violations. The primary architectural concern is that App.tsx functions as a hub module (407 LOC, ~85% of production code) combining scene data, UI components, and scroll-driven state management -- creating a moderate blast radius where changes to any aspect of the presentation layer route through this single module.
cross_module_architecture.score_rationale: The architecture is fundamentally sound for a project of this size (4 files, 479 LOC): dependency direction is clear, boundaries are respected, and there is no cross-module coordination through shared mutable state. The score of 78 reflects that a new team member would understand the structure in seconds, but is moderated by the App.tsx hub module which blurs the boundary between data/config and presentation.

issues.suggestion: Extract the scenes data array and hardcoded color palette into a separate data file (e.g. src/data/scenes.ts or src/data/site-content.ts). This separates configuration/presentation data from rendering logic and reduces the blast radius for content changes.

root_causes: Project is in early/prototype stage where rapid iteration favored monolithic structure over decomposition
